primary_text_note: In copyright. Verified against the Delaney manuscript held by the British Library (archive.org/details/atasteofhoneyw.rededits) plus LitCharts, GradeSaver, Revision World, Wikipedia, Britannica and the HarperCollins revision guide. The manuscript predates Littlewood's rehearsal edits, so absence from it alone was never treated as proof of fabrication.

findings.evidence: specs/aqa/english-literature-8702-8702.md §'Specification at a glance' — Paper 2, 2h15, 96 marks; 'Section A Modern texts: students will answer one essay question from a choice of two'; 'All assessments are closed book'.

findings.claim: KC[1] 'How many marks is each part of the Eduqas question on A Taste of Honey worth?' keyed to '20 marks each'.

findings.claim: All 48 practice questions are labelled '20 marks — Extract Analysis' or '20 marks — Wider Text Response', carry '[20 marks]' in the stem and a 1–20 band ladder. 17 of them begin 'Read the passage/extract…' and require a printed extract.
findings.truth: AQA Paper 2 Section A is one closed-book essay from a choice of two, 30 marks + 4 SPaG. Every question relabelled '30 marks — Modern Text Essay'; stems rescaled to [30 marks]; the 17 extract-dependent stems rewritten as whole-play essay questions; band ladders rescaled (25–30 / 19–24 / 13–18 / 7–12 / 1–6) with the 4 SPaG marks added.

findings.claim: The lesson says 18 in four places (description 'an 18-year-old’s play', conclusion 'aged 18', flashcard 'Eighteen.', knowledge check keyed to '18') but its own Key Fact says 'just 19 years old'.
findings.truth: Delaney was 19. She was born 25 November 1938 and wrote the play in 1958; it premiered 27 May 1958. '19' is the figure used by Wikipedia and Britannica.
findings.evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Taste_of_Honey ('written when she was 19'); https://www.britannica.com/biography/Shelagh-Delaney

findings.claim: 'He is never given a name in the play' / 'The Boy is never named in the play' — repeated in content, Key Fact, conclusion, a knowledge check and two flashcards, plus 'Unnamed tenderness' in a L5 matching item.
findings.truth: The Boy IS named. The script's speech prefix stays 'BOY', but Jo says his name — Jimmie — in Act 2, Scene 2. He is also 22 and a former nurse. The 'near-namelessness' reading survives; the absolute claim does not.
findings.evidence: https://www.litcharts.com/lit/a-taste-of-honey/act-1-scene-2 and https://www.gradesaver.com/a-taste-of-honey/study-guide/character-list — 'listed in the playscript as “The Boy”… not until Act 2, Scene 2 does Jo reveal his name is Jimmie'; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Taste_of_Honey names 'Jimmy, a black sailor'.

findings.claim: 'Jo’s first line, “The roof’s leaking”…' — repeated in the Key Fact, a flashcard and a knowledge check whose stem asks 'What is Jo’s first line in the play?'
findings.truth: The play opens HELEN: 'Well! This is the place.' / JO: 'And I don’t like it.' 'The roof’s leaking!' comes later in the same scene (Helen answers 'it’s just condensation'). The quotation is real; calling it Jo’s first line is not. None of the knowledge-check options held the true first line, so the stem was rewritten rather than the key.
findings.evidence: https://www.gradesaver.com/a-taste-of-honey/study-guide/quotes (Act One, Scene One opening); https://www.litcharts.com/lit/a-taste-of-honey/quotes

findings.claim: 'When Jo says “You’re just like a big sister,” Geof replies: “I’d sooner be more to you than that.”' — also quoted in L7 content, a L7 flashcard and a L7 mark scheme.
findings.truth: The exchange runs the other way and Geof’s line is different. GEOF: 'I’d sooner be dead than away from you.' JO (laughing): 'You’re just like a big sister to me.'
findings.evidence: Delaney manuscript (British Library, via archive.org/details/atasteofhoneyw.rededits) line 1365 'Geo. I’d sooner be dead than away from you.'; corroborated by https://quizlet.com/gb/296737343/ and https://www.gradesaver.com/a-taste-of-honey/study-guide/summary-act-two-scene-one

findings.claim: 'The dream has gone but the baby is real' — used in L4 content, Key Fact, revision prompt, conclusion, a knowledge check key and a flashcard; L5 attributes it to Jo ('What does Jo mean by…').
findings.truth: The line is Geof’s and the wording is 'Oh well, the dream’s gone, but the baby’s real enough.' The lesson’s version is the Smiths’ paraphrase (This Night Has Opened My Eyes), not Delaney’s text.
findings.evidence: https://clip.cafe/a-taste-of-honey-1961/oh-well-the-dreams-gone-but-the-babys-real-enough/ ; https://www.litcharts.com/lit/a-taste-of-honey/act-2-scene-2

findings.claim: Jo 'directly asks him about it: “Are you really a homosexual?”' — repeated in L7 content, a L7 flashcard and a L7 practice-question stem.
findings.truth: Fabricated. The word 'homosexual' never appears in the play. Jo presses Geof about why his landlady evicted him ('Does she think you’re — you know —') and about why he 'carries on' as he does; Geof answers around it. The claim that Jo is blunt about his sexuality is sound; the quotation is not.
findings.evidence: Delaney manuscript (archive.org/details/atasteofhoneyw.rededits) — zero hits for 'homosexual'; Geof's reply is 'I wasn’t born queer'. https://www.litcharts.com/lit/a-taste-of-honey/act-2-scene-1 records the interrogation without the word.

findings.claim: Helen 'calls him a “pansified little freak”' (content ×2 and a flashcard keyed to 'Little freak').
findings.truth: Misattributed. 'Simpering pansified little freaks' is JO’s phrase, used to DEFEND Geof against Helen. Helen’s own insults are 'What an arty little freak' and 'a bloody little pansy' (and, to his face, 'you pansified little apology for a man').
findings.evidence: https://www.litcharts.com/lit/a-taste-of-honey/quotes (HELEN: 'What an arty little freak!'); https://www.litcharts.com/lit/a-taste-of-honey/act-2-scene-2 ('a bloody little pansy'); manuscript line 1707 'Jos. …he isn’t like some of these simpering pansified little freaks…'

findings.claim: 'When he calls Jo “that ugly-looking thing,” Helen does not defend her daughter' — plus a fill-blank knowledge check keyed to 'thing', and loose 'Peter calling her ugly' claims in L3 and L5.
findings.truth: Fabricated — no trace in the Delaney manuscript, LitCharts, GradeSaver, Course Hero, Revision World or Goodreads, and no exact-phrase web hit. The moment is real but the words are different, and the speaker is Helen: Peter wants Jo out of the way, and HELEN tells Jo to 'turn yourself into a bloody termite and crawl into the wall or something' (Act 1, Scene 1). REPLACED with Helen's verified line, which carries the same point about Helen failing to defend her daughter; the knowledge check is rebuilt around 'termite' (keyed index unchanged). The two loose 'Peter calling her ugly' claims are de-quoted.
findings.evidence: https://www.litcharts.com/lit/a-taste-of-honey/act-1-scene-1 and https://www.gradesaver.com/a-taste-of-honey/study-guide/summary-act-one-scene-one — Act 1, Scene 1.

findings.claim: 'We’re all out of the same cup' — the unit's most-used quotation: L2 content and conclusion, L5 content, L7 content (staged as a verbatim exchange with an invented reply, JO: 'Yes, and it’s a very dirty cup'), L8 content, three knowledge checks, four flashcards, and the L8 exam tip that tells students to MEMORISE it.
findings.truth: Fabricated — no trace in the Delaney manuscript or in any quotation bank (LitCharts, GradeSaver, Course Hero, Revision World, Vaia, Goodreads), and no exact-phrase web hit. REPLACED throughout with Helen's verified line 'we all end up same way sooner or later' (Act 1, Scene 1), which carries exactly the shared-fate meaning the lessons need. Both fill-blank knowledge checks were rebuilt so the keyed index still lands on the real word ('later', 'way'). The fabricated L7 exchange — invented on both sides — is replaced with a verified set-up/knock-down pair, HELEN: 'You’re man mad.' JO: 'I’m like you.' (Act 2, Scene 1), and the surrounding analysis and scene reference rewritten to match.
findings.evidence: https://www.litcharts.com/lit/a-taste-of-honey/characters/helen — Act 1 Scene 1 p.13: 'Still, we all have funny ideas at that age, don’t we—makes no difference though, we all end up same way sooner or later.'; Act 2 Scene 1 p.62: HELEN 'You’re man mad.' / JO 'I’m like you.'

findings.claim: 'Oh well, it’s a lovely morning for it' — presented as Helen's signature deflection in L2, L4, L5 and L7, plus a L7 knowledge check built entirely on it, two flashcards, a L4 distractor and a L7 mark scheme.
findings.truth: Fabricated — no trace in the manuscript or in any quotation bank, and no exact-phrase web hit. REPLACED in L5, L7 (content, knowledge check, mark scheme), the L5 flashcard and the L4 distractor with Helen's verified deflection 'Have I ever laid claim to being a proper mother?' (Act 1, Scene 2). In L2, where the slot is Jo complaining about the flat, replaced with Helen's verified Act 1 Scene 1 joke: they have 'no heating — but there’s a lovely view of the gasworks'. The L4 sentence claims the line RESURFACES in Act 2; no verified line does, so that one sentence is DE-QUOTED and now describes Helen's deflecting humour without quoting.
findings.evidence: https://www.litcharts.com/lit/a-taste-of-honey/characters/helen — Act 1 Scene 2 p.35: 'Have I ever laid claim to being a proper mother?'; https://www.litcharts.com/lit/a-taste-of-honey/quotes — Act 1 Scene 1: 'Everything in it’s falling apart, it’s true, and we’ve no heating—but there’s a lovely view of the gasworks…'

findings.claim: The glossary pop-up and glossary entry define 'abandonment' as 'A recurring event, image, or idea that develops significance through repetition across a text.'
findings.truth: That is the definition of a MOTIF. L2 defines the same term correctly ('The state of being cast off or left behind, a recurring experience for Jo throughout the play'), so the unit contradicts itself.
findings.evidence: Internal: L2 glossary_terms entry for the same term.

findings.claim: 'The entire play takes place in one location: a rented flat in Salford.'
findings.truth: Two small imprecisions. The single set is the flat AND the street outside — Delaney's only description is that it 'represents a comfortless flat … and the street outside'. And the city is disputed: the note at the front of the first edition says Salford, while the opening stage direction says Manchester. The 'single set' claim itself is correct and the Salford reading is the standard teaching line, so no edit.
findings.evidence: https://harpercollins.co.uk/blogs/features/revision-guide-a-taste-of-honey

findings.claim: 'Peter has thrown her out, and she needs Jo’s flat as a refuge' (also a keyed knowledge-check option, a flashcard, and L5 'When he eventually throws Helen out').
findings.truth: Peter leaves Helen for another woman; Helen turns up at Jo’s flat with her cases. She is not evicted by him.
findings.evidence: https://www.litcharts.com/lit/a-taste-of-honey/act-2-scene-2 — 'Peter left her for another woman.'

findings.claim: Practice Q1: 'Read the passage where Jo tells Geof “I’m not just talented, I’m geniused.”'
findings.truth: Jo says it to HELEN, in Act 1, Scene 1, when Helen praises her drawing. Geof does not appear until Act 2, so the moment described cannot exist. The quotation itself is correct.
findings.evidence: Delaney manuscript line 160 — 'Hel. …I didn’t realise I had such a talented young daughter. / Jos. I’m not that talented – I’m geniused.' (published wording 'I’m not just talented, I’m geniused'); https://www.litcharts.com/lit/a-taste-of-honey/characters/jo

findings.claim: 'For a girl whose mother calls her “useless”…'
findings.truth: 'You really are useless, Jo' is GEOF’s line in Act 2, said affectionately about her cooking. It is not Helen’s, and it is not in Act 1. Helen does belittle Jo’s looks ('the most clumsy, awkward, shapeless lump of a girl I ever came across'), so the point survives without the misattributed quotation.
findings.evidence: Delaney manuscript line 1145 'Geo. …you really are useless, Jo.'; https://revisionworld.com/level-revision/english-literature-gcse-level/taste-honey-shelagh-delaney/quotes-taste-honey

findings.claim: 'She tells Helen: “You’re just a selfish old woman.”'
findings.truth: Unverified — no hit in the manuscript or in any quotation bank. REPLACED with Jo's verified line 'You hurt people’s feelings and you don’t even notice' (Act 2, Scene 2), which serves the same point about Jo's bluntness towards her mother.
findings.evidence: https://www.litcharts.com/lit/a-taste-of-honey/characters/jo — Act 2 Scene 2 p.79: 'You hurt people’s feelings and you don’t even notice.'

summary: All 8 lessons carry findings. The unit was written to the wrong exam: every practice question is a 20-mark extract/wider-text pair, six lessons refer to 'part (a)' or 'part (b)', and L8 names Eduqas and teaches a printed extract - AQA 8702 Paper 2 Section A is one closed-book 30-mark essay (+4 SPaG, AO1 12 / AO2 12 / AO3 6). AO4 is defined as context (AO3's job) in two glossaries. Ten quotations are fabricated, misworded or misattributed, including four the exam tip told students to memorise; every one is now replaced with wording verified by act and scene, except a single L4 sentence that claimed a line recurs in Act 2, which is de-quoted. No fabricated quotation remains in the unit.
